The flaw allows an attacker who has already achieved prototype pollution in the same process to inject arbitrary HTTP headers into outgoing Axios requests by exploiting the dispatchRequest() function's normalization of inherited Object.prototype.headers. It was published on September 28, 2026, and fixed in version 1.20.0. The vulnerability carries a CVSS v4.0 base score of 6.9 (Medium) (GitHub Advisory, Red Hat). Technical details The root cause lies in lib/core/dispatchRequest.js, which contains the statement config.headers = AxiosHeaders.from(config.headers);. The initial merged config object uses a null prototype (hardened against prototype pollution), but a request interceptor can replace it with a plain JavaScript object. If that replacement object lacks an own headers property, the property read resolves up the prototype chain to Object.prototype.headers — which an attacker may have previously polluted via a separate vulnerability. This is classified as CWE-1321 (Prototype Pollution), CWE-915 (Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes), and CWE-74 (Injection). Three preconditions must be met: (1) a separate prototype-pollution primitive must have written an object to Object.prototype.headers, (2) the application must use a request interceptor that returns a replacement config object without an own headers property, and (3) the Axios version must be 1.0.0–1.19.x. A complete proof-of-concept is publicly available in the GitHub Security Advisory (GitHub Advisory, Red Hat Bugzilla). Impact Successful exploitation allows an attacker to inject arbitrary HTTP headers — including authorization-related values — into outgoing Axios requests made by the vulnerable application. Depending on the downstream service receiving those requests, this can result in cache poisoning, conditional-request suppression (e.g., via If-None-Match: *), metadata-service header injection (e.g., cloud IMDS endpoints), or application-specific authorization bypass and routing manipulation. The primary impact is on integrity of subsequent systems (rated High in CVSS v4.0), with a low confidentiality impact on subsequent systems; the vulnerable system itself has no direct confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact. This allows attacker-controlled request headers, including authorization-related values, to be observed by downstream request handling logic. Affected Versions Affected versions: 1.0.0 to 1.20.0 Fixed versions: 1.20.0 Details Trigger Conditions: An independent prototype pollution vulnerability exists within the same process, injecting malicious data into Object.prototype.headers. Propagation Path: A trusted request interceptor intercepts the request and returns a new plain configuration object without an own headers property. This configuration object is passed to dispatchRequest after being processed through the interceptor chain. Vulnerability Principle: When normalizing the configuration, if dispatchRequest does not find an own headers property, it searches up the prototype chain, thereby reading the polluted global Object.prototype.headers. Result: During downstream request handling, the headers object contains data controlled by the attacker. Impact Security Risk: Attackers can inject malicious HTTP request headers.
